cues.en: We can still call this an averaging machine.

cues.en: I'm basically just writing it out in a slightly different way compared to the previous slide.
cues.zh: 只是和上一張投影片相比，換了一種寫法。

cues.en: By the way.
cues.zh: 順便說，

cues.zh: 注意這裡的數學運算。

cues.en: And then summing up all of the element wise multiplications together.
cues.zh: 再把所有逐元素乘積加起來。

cues.en: Okay we're going to I'm going to come back to that point in a moment.
cues.zh: 稍後會回到這一點。

cues.en: First I want to explore the idea of taking weighted sums of the inputs.
cues.zh: 先探索對輸入取加權總和的概念。

cues.en: So now what I'm doing is just changing the the weight values.
cues.zh: 現在，我只改變權重值。

cues.en: So this is the same.
cues.zh: 這一部分仍然相同。

cues.en: This is still just a summation here.
cues.zh: 仍然只是加總。

cues.en: We still have weights one weight per input number.
cues.zh: 仍然有權重，每個輸入數字對應一個權重。

cues.en: But I've just changed the numbers now.
cues.zh: 只是數值改變了。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So this would we can express this mathematically like this.
cues.zh: 可以像這樣用數學表示。

cues.en: So it's still the input number times the weight plus the input number times weight plus the input number times weight.
cues.zh: 仍然是輸入乘以權重，再加輸入乘以權重，再加輸入乘以權重。

cues.en: So and well in this case this is not an averaging machine.
cues.zh: 不過，現在不是一般的平均計算機。

cues.en: We can call this a weighted averaging machine because we are still computing some kind of an average.

cues.en: but we are weighting the different inputs according to these little W's over here.

cues.en: Maybe it would be better to call this a weighted sum compared to weighted average, because the word average already implies a particular, um, operation.
cues.zh: 或許叫加權總和，比加權平均更好，因為平均這個詞已經隱含特定運算。

cues.en: So let's call let's start calling this a weighted sum.
cues.zh: 所以，開始把它叫做加權總和。

cues.en: We are summing up all of these numbers, but we're not summing them directly.
cues.zh: 把這些數字加起來，但不是直接相加。

cues.en: We are waiting them first by some additional numbers here, which I call w.
cues.zh: 而是先用我稱為 w 的額外數字來加權。

cues.en: So now let's get back to this concept of what this operation really means.
cues.zh: 回到這個概念：這項運算究竟代表什麼？

cues.en: So we're taking these three numbers and these three weights and element wise multiplying them and then summing them together.
cues.zh: 取這三個數字與三個權重，逐元素相乘，再加總。

cues.en: And that gives us a single number.
cues.zh: 得到一個數字。

cues.en: Now I hope that sounds familiar from the uh, a couple sections ago about the math prerequisites, in particular the lecture for the dot product.
cues.zh: 希望這聽起來很熟悉，前幾節數學先備知識，尤其是內積那堂課，已經介紹過。

cues.en: In fact, what we are doing here is computing the dot product between a vector x that is the inputs And a vector w that contains the weights.
cues.zh: 實際上，我們正在計算輸入向量 x，和包含權重的向量 w 之間的內積。

cues.en: So we can write this out as.
cues.zh: 可以寫成這樣。

cues.en: The output of the model is a value y.
cues.zh: 模型的輸出，是一個 y 值。

cues.en: We call this variable y and it just equals the dot product between x the vector of inputs, and w the vector of weights.
cues.zh: 把變數叫做 y，它等於輸入向量 x 與權重向量 w 的內積。

cues.en: So x transpose w that is the dot product.
cues.zh: 也就是 x 轉置乘以 w，代表內積。

cues.en: And that is literally what this machine is doing.
cues.zh: 這正是這台機器做的事。

cues.en: Now this is a linear operation with animation because it's a pretty important concept.
cues.zh: 這是線性運算，我還加上動畫，因為這是很重要的概念。

cues.en: This is a linear operation that we are implementing here.
cues.zh: 我們在這裡實作的是線性運算。

cues.en: So let me talk for a moment about linear and nonlinear operations.
cues.zh: 簡短談一下線性與非線性運算。

cues.en: A linear operation just means that you are doing addition and scalar multiplication.
cues.zh: 線性運算指的，就是加法與純量乘法。

cues.en: So if your mathematical operation simply involves addition and scalar multiplication, then it's a linear operation.
cues.zh: 如果數學運算只涉及加法與純量乘法，就是線性運算。

cues.en: And anything else is basically nonlinear.
cues.zh: 其他基本上都是非線性。

cues.en: So linear means addition and multiplication.
cues.zh: 所以，線性就是加法與乘法。

cues.en: You could draw straight lines through the output, and non-linear is anything else where you don't have straight lines, you don't have just addition and multiplication.
cues.zh: 可以用直線描述輸出；非線性則是其他情況，不是直線，也不只是加法與乘法。

cues.en: This issue of linear versus non-linear is going to come up fairly often in the next couple sections, in particular later videos.
cues.zh: 接下來幾節，尤其後面幾支影片，會經常談線性與非線性。

cues.en: In this section, I'm going to show you examples of linear problems and non-linear problems, linear solutions or I should say linear models and non-linear models.
cues.zh: 這一節會示範線性與非線性問題，以及線性解，或者應該說，線性模型與非線性模型。

cues.en: And I'll discuss why we need linear models for linear problems.
cues.zh: 也會討論，為什麼線性問題需要線性模型。

cues.en: You'll see examples of this and so on.
cues.zh: 你會看到相關例子。

cues.en: But for now, suffice it to say that linear models can only solve linearly separable problems.
cues.zh: 目前只要知道，線性模型只能解決線性可分的問題。

cues.en: Linearly separable problems are problems where you can achieve the result by drawing a straight line through the two different groups.
cues.zh: 線性可分，就是可以在兩組之間畫一條直線，達成分類目標。

cues.en: I'll show an example of this on the next slide.
cues.zh: 下一張投影片會示範。

cues.en: So linear models are actually not very good at solving Non-linearly separable problems, so non-linear models can solve more complex problems.
cues.zh: 所以，線性模型其實不太擅長解決線性不可分的問題，而非線性模型能解決更複雜的問題。

cues.en: Linear models can only solve linearly separable problems.
cues.zh: 線性模型只能解決線性可分問題。

cues.en: This also means that you shouldn't use a linear model for a nonlinear problem, and you also, as it turns out, shouldn't use a non-linear model for a linear problem.
cues.zh: 這也代表，不應該用線性模型解非線性問題；而且你會看到，也不應該用非線性模型解線性問題。

cues.en: Now, linear models are what you come across in a standards course on statistics and machine learning.
cues.zh: 線性模型，就是標準統計與機器學習課程裡會遇到的。

cues.en: Things like regression, general linear models, Anova.
cues.zh: 例如迴歸、一般線性模型，以及變異數分析。

cues.en: These are all factor analysis.
cues.zh: 還有因素分析。

cues.en: These are all examples of linear models.
cues.zh: 這些都是線性模型的例子。

cues.en: Now linear models are really great.
cues.zh: 線性模型真的很好。

cues.en: And there are lots and lots of linearly separable problems in the universe.
cues.zh: 宇宙裡有很多線性可分問題。

cues.en: And we use linear models for them.
cues.zh: 我們就用線性模型處理。

cues.en: Any kind of general variant of a general linear model.
cues.zh: 也就是各種一般線性模型的變體。

cues.en: But there are also many problems that cannot be solved through linear models.
cues.zh: 但也有很多問題，無法用線性模型解決。

cues.en: And that's why we need nonlinear operations in our deep learning models.
cues.zh: 所以，深度學習模型裡需要非線性運算。

cues.en: And then also the second part of the statement.
cues.zh: 還有剛才敘述的第二部分。

cues.en: Not to use a nonlinear model for a linear problem.
cues.zh: 不要用非線性模型解線性問題。

cues.en: I will also show an example of this in in a video later on in this section.
cues.zh: 這一節後面的影片，也會舉例。

cues.en: Essentially, the idea is that if you use a nonlinear model, the added complexity generally just makes things more complicated.
cues.zh: 基本概念是，如果使用非線性模型，額外的複雜度通常只會把事情弄得更複雜。

cues.en: A linear solution is going to be a better fit for a linear problem.
cues.zh: 線性解比較適合線性問題。

cues.zh: 好的。

cues.zh: 取輸入，乘上權重，再加總。

cues.zh: 是線性的。

cues.en: Nonetheless, this is a really simple nonlinear function to illustrate for our purposes here, of introducing
cues.zh: 不過，拿這個簡單非線性函式來示範，很適合目前的目的，

cues.en: you to the idea of computing a linear weighted sum of inputs and passing that value through some nonlinear function.

cues.zh: 再次說明，就是輸入值乘上對應權重。

cues.en: And then we sum all of those together.
cues.zh: 然後全部加起來。

cues.en: This is a linear operation.
cues.zh: 這是線性運算。

cues.en: And this result gets passed through this uh this other function here which is a nonlinear Non-linear function.
cues.zh: 接著，結果送進另一個非線性函式。

cues.en: It's commonly called an activation function, but it just has some non-linearity built into it.
cues.zh: 通常叫做活化函式，裡面包含某種非線性。

cues.en: Now there's one extra piece to the perceptron, to the basic unit of the Ann that I haven't yet told you about.
cues.zh: 感知器，也就是 ANN 的基本單位，還有一個尚未介紹的小部分。

cues.en: And that little piece is called the bias term.
cues.zh: 叫做偏置項。

cues.en: If you have a statistics background, if you've taken a statistics course, the bias term is also called an intercept.
cues.zh: 如果你有統計背景、上過統計課，偏置也叫做截距。

cues.en: It's exactly the same thing as an intercept in a general linear model or a regression.
cues.zh: 和一般線性模型或迴歸裡的截距，完全是同一件事。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So to introduce you to the to or to motivate why we need a bias term, I want you to draw a line.
cues.zh: 為了介紹偏置，或者說明為什麼需要它，請你畫一條線。

cues.en: Draw a straight line that separates the green dots from the blue dots.
cues.zh: 畫一條直線，把綠色點和藍色點分開。

cues.en: Now obviously this is a really simple problem.
cues.zh: 很明顯，這非常簡單。

cues.en: In fact, this is an example of a linearly separable problem.
cues.zh: 其實，這就是線性可分的例子。

cues.en: This is a linearly separable problem because we can draw a straight line that perfectly separates the two populations of colors here.
cues.zh: 因為可以畫一條直線，把兩組不同顏色的點完美分開。

cues.en: Okay, how about here?
cues.zh: 這裡呢？

cues.en: Is it still possible to draw a line that separates these two colors?
cues.zh: 還能畫一條線，分開這兩種顏色嗎？

cues.en: Now, I know you're thinking that this is really trivial because the answer is yeah, of course.
cues.zh: 我知道你覺得很簡單，答案當然是可以。

cues.en: You just draw a line through here.
cues.zh: 只要在這裡畫一條線。

cues.en: But what if I said that that line must pass through the origin of the graph.
cues.zh: 但如果規定，這條線必須經過座標原點呢？

cues.en: So here's the origin.
cues.zh: 這裡是原點。

cues.en: This dot here.
cues.zh: 就是這個點。

cues.en: So the line that best separates these two groups of dots must pass through the origin.
cues.zh: 最能分開這兩組點的直線，必須經過原點。

cues.en: Well you know that line is going to go like this.
cues.zh: 那麼，直線就會像這樣。

cues.en: And this is the best we can possibly do.
cues.zh: 這已經是能做到的最佳情況。

cues.en: It's actually not so bad.
cues.zh: 其實也不算太差。

cues.en: We're still getting, you know, the majority of the blue dots on this side, the majority of the green dots on this side.
cues.zh: 大部分藍色點仍然在這邊，大部分綠色點在另一邊。

cues.en: But obviously this is not the optimal solution.
cues.zh: 但很明顯，這不是最佳解。

cues.en: Now why do we have to confine this line to go through the origin.
cues.zh: 為什麼必須限制直線通過原點？

cues.en: Well this is what the model looks like if we do not include a bias term.
cues.zh: 如果不加入偏置項，模型就會是這個樣子。

cues.en: So instead we want to include a bias term in the model and the bias term, or the intercept basically
cues.zh: 所以，想在模型裡加入偏置，也就是截距，

cues.en: allows the line to go off the origin, not to pass through the origin.
cues.zh: 讓直線可以離開原點，不必通過原點。

cues.en: And then having a bias term gives us the opportunity to draw separating hyperplanes or lines that can pass through the y axis anywhere.
cues.zh: 有了偏置，就能畫出在 y 軸任意位置通過的分隔超平面或直線。

cues.en: They don't need to pass through the origin.
cues.zh: 不必通過原點。

cues.en: Okay, so this model has no bias term.
cues.zh: 這個模型沒有偏置項。

cues.en: This model has a bias term or an intercept.
cues.zh: 這個模型則有偏置，也就是截距。

cues.en: Now do you always need to have a bias term.
cues.zh: 一定都需要偏置項嗎？

cues.en: Well you don't necessarily always need a bias term.
cues.zh: 不一定每次都需要。

cues.en: You can actually transform the data to be mean centered.
cues.zh: 其實，可以先把資料轉換成以平均數為中心。

cues.en: So you can mean center the data, subtract the mean from the data along all dimensions, and then you're still going to be okay.
cues.zh: 沿所有維度減掉平均數、做中心化，這樣也能處理。

cues.en: You're still going to have the the separating line pass through the origin.
cues.zh: 分隔線仍然可以通過原點。

cues.en: However this is not really something we want to rely on.
cues.zh: 但這不是我們真正想依賴的方法。

cues.en: So instead we just always add a bias term.
cues.zh: 所以，直接一律加入偏置。

cues.en: Now why is this the case mathematically?
cues.zh: 數學上，為什麼會這樣？

cues.en: Where does the bias term come up mathematically?
cues.zh: 偏置項，在數學上是怎麼出現的？

cues.en: Well this line here can be represented as y equals mx.
cues.zh: 這條線可以表示成 y=mx。

cues.en: So m is the slope of the line and x is the x axis and y is the y axis.
cues.zh: m 是斜率，x 對應 x 軸，y 對應 y 軸。

cues.en: So if this is our formula then when x equals zero y must also equal zero.
cues.zh: 如果公式是這樣，x 等於零時，y 也必須為零。

cues.en: It doesn't matter what m is m can be any possible value.
cues.zh: 不管 m 是多少，任何數值都一樣。

cues.en: And as long as x equals zero y must also equal zero.
cues.zh: 只要 x 等於零，y 就必須為零。

cues.en: So this equation must or any line that's define any model that's characterized by this equation must go through the origin the 00..
cues.zh: 所以，任何由這個方程式定義的直線、模型，都必須經過原點零、零。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So then we can what we do is we add this B term here.
cues.zh: 接著，我們加入 b 這一項。

cues.en: So this is the bias also called the intercept term in statistics.
cues.zh: 就是偏置，在統計裡也叫截距項。

cues.en: So now this is a very familiar looking equation.
cues.zh: 現在，這是很熟悉的方程式。

cues.en: Of course you know this from middle school.
cues.zh: 當然，你國中就學過。

cues.en: y equals mx plus b.
cues.zh: y=mx+b。

cues.en: So now we can set x to be zero.
cues.zh: 把 x 設為零。

cues.en: And and then y equals b when x is zero.
cues.zh: x 等於零時，y 就等於 b。

cues.en: So now you know in this plot let's say b equals you know I don't know numbers on here.
cues.zh: 這張圖裡，假設 b 等於——我沒有標數字。

cues.en: But let's just say this is five.
cues.zh: 就假設這裡是五。

cues.en: So now when x equals zero y equals b.
cues.zh: x 等於零時，y 等於 b。

cues.en: And we set that to be five.
cues.zh: 而 b 設成五。

cues.en: So we need the bias term in the model in order to avoid having this kind of an awkward situation where
cues.zh: 所以，需要偏置項，避免這種尷尬情況，

cues.en: we are going to get a suboptimal result simply because the line is constrained to pass through the origin.
cues.zh: 也就是只因直線被限制通過原點，就得到次佳結果。

cues.en: So this is why we need a bias term.
cues.zh: 這就是需要偏置的原因。

cues.en: Now, I mentioned here, you know, if you mean center everything, you can get away without a bias term.
cues.zh: 前面提過，如果全部做平均中心化，可以不加偏置。

cues.en: But this is this is more for like academic elucidation.
cues.zh: 但這比較偏學術上的說明。

cues.en: In practice you always include a bias term.
cues.zh: 實務上，總是加入偏置項。

cues.en: Fortunately, when we start working with PyTorch, you will see that including the bias term is the default procedure in PyTorch, so you don't really have to worry about adding it explicitly.
cues.zh: 幸好，開始使用 PyTorch 後，你會看到，加入偏置是預設做法，所以不必特別手動加上。

cues.en: It is important, however, to know that it exists and why we need it.
cues.zh: 但仍然需要知道，它存在，以及為什麼需要它。

cues.en: Okay, so that means that the graph our graph actually looks something like this.
cues.zh: 好的，所以，我們的示意圖其實像這樣。

cues.en: We have our input numbers and the bias term here.
cues.zh: 這裡有輸入數字，以及偏置。

cues.en: And these all feed into the operation or the computation node over here.
cues.zh: 全部送進這邊的運算、計算節點。

cues.en: So then mathematically it's you know this is what I drew before.
cues.zh: 數學上，這是前面畫的。

cues.en: This is what I wrote out before.
cues.zh: 也是前面寫出的式子。

cues.en: In fact it looks more like this.
cues.zh: 但實際上，更像這樣。

cues.en: So we have all of the input values.
cues.zh: 先有全部輸入值。

cues.en: These are the numbers the inputs to the model.
cues.zh: 也就是模型的數字輸入。

cues.en: And we have their corresponding weights.
cues.zh: 再有各自對應的權重。

cues.en: And then we have one extra set here we have an extra term for the bias and then for the weight of the bias.
cues.zh: 另外多出一組，也就是偏置，以及偏置的權重。

cues.en: Now the thing is we can set this bias to be any value we want.
cues.zh: 可以把這個偏置輸入設成任意值。

cues.en: And this w zero is going to be a parameter that the model optimizes.
cues.zh: w_0 則是模型會最佳化的參數。

cues.en: So because these are just two constants that are multiplying each other.
cues.zh: 因為這裡只是兩個常數相乘，

cues.en: Then in practice, what we do is we just set the bias term to be one, which means implicitly we drop it out of the equation.
cues.zh: 實務上直接把偏置輸入設成一，等於在式子裡省略它。

cues.en: So implicitly we we the bias gets removed and we just have this w0.
cues.zh: 所以，隱含把那個偏置輸入省略，只留下 w_0。

cues.en: Again we need this w0.
cues.zh: 再次強調，需要這個 w_0。

cues.en: This is a bias or intercept term that allows us to fit any arbitrary data positioned anywhere in the plane.
cues.zh: 這是偏置或截距，讓我們能擬合放在平面任意位置的資料。
